title: Photoactivation of YAP in Cancer Cell Spheroids Embedded in Collagen Gels
author: Illes, Engelke

steps.title: Generate HeLa spheroids in low‑adhesion plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 HeLa cells into each well of a low‑adhesion 96‑well plate containing 100 µL DMEM (10 % FBS, 1 % Pen‑Strep) and incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to form spheroids (~250 µm diameter).

steps.title: Prepare collagen gel and embed spheroids
steps.instruction: On ice, prepare a 200 µL collagen‑I gel per well, embed two spheroids, gelate, and verify integrity.

substeps.instruction: Place 150 µL collagen Type I solution (8.35 mg/mL) in an Eppendorf tube on ice.
Prepare NaOH/PBS mix: 2.5 µL 1 M NaOH + 47.5 µL PBS per well, keep on ice.
Combine the collagen solution with the NaOH/PBS mix, gently pipette up/down ≈3 times, and dispense 200 µL into each well of an ibidi 8‑well µ‑slide.

Collect spheroids and surrounding medium from the low‑adhesion plate with disposable plastic pipettes and add two spheroids to each well; adjust total volume to 400 µL per well (add fresh medium if needed).
Optional: gently mix the gel after adding spheroids.
Verify that the final pH is ~7.4; adjust with additional NaOH if necessary to obtain a final collagen concentration of 3.13 mg/mL.
Place the slide in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for 30 min to allow gelation.
Inspect the embedded spheroids under a light microscope; if they appear undamaged, proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Transfect embedded spheroids with optoYAP
steps.instruction: Prepare transfection mix, add to each well together with photocaged lysine, and incubate.

substeps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL tube, prepare 100 µL transfection mixture (per 8‑well slide, with excess): 1 µg optoYAP plasmid, 1 µg PAG plasmid, 3 µL Xtreme Gene 9 reagent, and bring to 100 µL with Opti‑MEM.
Tap the tube to mix and incubate 20 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C).
Add 10 µL of the transfection mixture to each well of the 8‑well slide.
Add 3 µL photocaged lysine per well (final concentration 0.75 µg/µL).
Incubate the slide at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for at least 24 h (optimal ≈36 h; do not exceed 48 h).

steps.title: Immunostain spheroids in collagen gel
steps.instruction: Perform fixation, permeabilization, blocking, antibody incubations, and nuclear staining while keeping samples wet.

substeps.instruction: Carefully remove medium from each well with a pipette.
Fix spheroids with 200 µL 4 % formaldehyde for 40 min at room temperature.
Wash twice with 300 µL cold PBS, 20 min each wash.
Permeabilize with 200 µL 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 20 min.
Wash with 300 µL PBS for 30 min.
Block with 200 µL PBS containing 1 % BSA overnight (10‑24 h).
Dilute 1 µg primary antibody in 200 µL PBS + 1 % BSA, add to wells, and incubate 72 h at 4 °C (or as specified).
Wash twice with 300 µL cold PBS, 20 min each.
Incubate with 1 µg secondary antibody in 200 µL PBS + 1 % BSA for 48 h.
Wash with 300 µL PBS for 20 min.
Stain nuclei with 0.5 µg/mL Hoechst in PBS for 40 min.
Wash with 300 µL PBS for 30 min.
Replace with fresh PBS, keep samples wet, store at 4 °C protected from light (stable for months).

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for photoactivation of Yes-associated protein with optoYAP. Particularly, it describes creating and embedding HeLa cell spheroids in collagen gels, their subsequent transfection with optoYAP plasmids, and the induction of directed growth by photoactivation of optoYAP. Furthermore, it presents an immunostaining procedure for spheroids in collagen gels. This protocol was also used for A431 cells and should also be usable for other cells that allow for the formation of stable spheroids and their transfection.
